note: Errata 29, which overturns 26 on the inventory. Verbs stay three columns of four on the left; the inventory is now a GRID OF ICONS on the right where the text list was, scroll arrows at the right edge, sentence line full width above. Geometry lives here rather than in Screen.ts because two things read it: the engine, and the Python that renders the panel for review.
errata54: Q35 AS RULED: the panel's type is at PANEL_GLYPH_SCALE 4, not the play area's 6, and these rows are authored for a 28-unit glyph. Errata 54 moved the panel from 320x56 to 1920x216, which is NOT the play area's exact 6x: 216/56 is 3.857, because the panel was re-proportioned rather than scaled -- that is how 1080 works at all, being 5.4x of 200. The face came along at 6x anyway, into the one region where 6 is provably the wrong factor, and five lines of 42-unit glyphs need 210 of 216 rows before a single gap. TALK TO and MENU were one unbroken 83-row run of ink and the last row ended one pixel from the frame; on a 1366x768 Chromebook, FIT-scaled to 0.711, that pixel is spent and MENU, MAP and FULL are cut off. At 4 the same five lines take 140 of 216 and leave 35.2% as leading, against the original 320x56 panel's 37.5%. What is preserved is the SHAPE errata 26 and 29 specify -- three columns of four verb cells, MENU and the map and fullscreen in the fourth row, a four-by-two inventory grid on the right, arrows at the right edge, sentence line full width above. Re-author these rows the day Q6's font lands; the scale is derived from the panel's own migration factor and will survive a face that keeps a 7-row cell.

verbs.note: SCUMM had twelve verbs in three columns of four. We have nine, per Bible v2, so the fourth row carries MENU, MAP and FULL instead of three more verbs -- the grid is the reference's shape and no cell is left empty. Pitch 42 against a 28-unit glyph is 14 units of leading, and a 33-unit cell centres the label at +2 by the same arithmetic the menu buttons use, so every label in the grid sits on one line.

inventory.note: Eight visible, the top of ruling 29's six-to-eight. Four columns across the right-hand block, two rows. The ITEM NAME still draws in the sentence line on hover and on selection -- ruling 29 condition 1, and it is not optional: an icon must never be the only way an item is identified, which is also why ruling 26's authored display names stand unchanged.

arrows.note: Drawn as triangles, not typed. A typed arrow would put an interface shape into the writing font -- true of the void 5x7 face and true of whatever replaces it.

mapButton.note: Doc 20 rule 2: the map is ALWAYS reachable. A hotspot in one room cannot satisfy that, so the map opens from the panel and not from a doorway. It sits in the verb grid's fourth row beside MENU, in geometry errata 26 already allocated and left empty -- nine verbs fill three rows of three, and the fourth row had one cell used and two spare.

fullscreenButton.note: ERRATA 39, as ruled. Its fullscreen toggle wants a control in the menu overlay AND in the verb panel, 'per the mouse-only requirement' -- a control reachable only behind another control is one indirection from mouse-complete, and errata 39 names both on purpose. This takes the verb grid's LAST FREE CELL: nine verbs fill three rows of three, and the fourth row held MENU and MAP with one spare. There is no spare now, which is worth knowing before the next thing wants one.
